page: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7i.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance across multiple categories. Its multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top 10% according to stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, reaching 454.59 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 190.44 GB/sec for write operations. This memory throughput supports high-performance database operations, as evidenced by top-tier Redis SET performance of 183.87 million operations per second and a top-tier static web serving throughput of 125.65 GB/sec. Additionally, the platform shows strong capabilities in large language model (LLM) inference, processing prompts at 234.96 tokens per second on medium 7B models and 37.79 tokens per second on large 70B models.

From a resource density perspective, the r7i.48xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise workloads by consolidating massive datasets into RAM, reducing the need for disk-based caching. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. With its 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this server is optimized for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
